general.q: Which is the longest river located entirely within Scotland?
general.why: The Tay flows for 117 miles across Scotland, edging out the Spey which reaches 107 miles.

general.q: Which gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
general.why: Nitrogen dominates our atmosphere, with oxygen making up almost all of the remaining 21%.

general.q: In which London street did the Great Fire of London begin in September 1666?
general.why: It started at Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane on 2 September 1666.

general.q: Which spirit forms the base of a classic Negroni cocktail, alongside Campari and sweet vermouth?
general.why: An equal-parts mix of gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth creates this iconic Italian cocktail.

general.q: Which English word for an order to stay indoors comes from the Old French for 'cover fire'?
general.why: It comes from 'couvre-feu', a medieval law requiring household fires to be extinguished at night.

pop.q: In classic 1990s Tomb Raider video games, what is the name of Lara Croft's long-suffering butler?
pop.why: Winston famously follows Lara around Croft Manor carrying his tray of tea, often getting locked in the freezer!

pop.q: In the 1990s playground craze Pogs, what were the heavier metal or plastic discs used to flip the caps called?
pop.why: Slammers were used to strike the stack of Pogs, and players kept any caps that landed face up!

pop.q: Which chocolate brand famously asked in its adverts: "Do you love anyone enough to give them your last...?"
pop.why: The iconic Rolo slogan ran from 1980 until 2003, featuring sweet clips of people giving away their final sweet.

pop.q: In the 1993 Wallace & Gromit film The Wrong Trousers, what disguise does Feathers McGraw wear to look like a chicken?
pop.why: Feathers McGraw puts a red rubber glove on his head to impersonate a chicken while committing diamond heists!

pop.q: In the BBC sitcom The Royle Family, what is lazy patriarch Jim Royle's signature catchphrase?
pop.why: Played by Ricky Tomlinson, Jim Royle yelled "My arse!" from his armchair at almost everything on TV.

music.q: What was the title of Radiohead's debut studio album, released in 1993?
music.why: 'Pablo Honey' launched Radiohead's career in 1993, driven by the breakout single 'Creep'.

music.q: Which synth-pop group, fronted by Martin Fry, released the hit 1982 album 'The Lexicon of Love'?
music.why: Produced by Trevor Horn, ABC's 'The Lexicon of Love' topped the UK Albums Chart in 1982.

music.q: Which song by Gnarls Barkley became the first single to reach UK Number 1 on downloads alone in 2006?
music.why: 'Crazy' spent nine consecutive weeks at UK Number 1 in 2006, making chart history.

music.q: Which American rock band beat Joe McElderry to the UK Christmas Number 1 spot in 2009?
music.why: 'Killing in the Name' won a famous fan campaign to keep The X Factor winner off the top spot.

music.q: On which Somerset farm has the Glastonbury Festival been held since its inception in 1970?
music.why: Michael Eavis hosted the first festival at his dairy farm, Worthy Farm, in September 1970.

mix.q: Which British band had a major hit in 1997 with the single 'Tubthumping'?
mix.why: Tubthumping reached number two in the UK Singles Chart in 1997.

mix.q: In the sitcom 'Spaced', what is the name of Tim and Daisy's eccentric landlady?
mix.why: Marsha Klein was memorably played by Julia Deakin in the Channel 4 comedy.

mix.q: Which 1990s English rock band was formed by brothers Richard and Danny McNamara?
mix.why: Embrace topped the UK album chart in 1998 with their debut album 'The Good Will Out'.

mix.q: Which traditional British dish consists of sausages baked in a savoury batter?
mix.why: Toad in the hole is traditionally served with onion gravy and vegetables.

mix.q: In the 1999 film 'Fight Club', which actor plays the character of Tyler Durden?
mix.why: Brad Pitt starred as soap maker Tyler Durden alongside Edward Norton.

mix.q: Which American rock group released the hit single 'Mr. Brightside' in 2003?
mix.why: The Killers released 'Mr. Brightside' as their debut single from the album 'Hot Fuss'.

mix.q: Which Roman emperor ordered the construction of a stone wall across northern Britain in AD 122?
mix.why: Hadrian's Wall stretched 73 miles from the River Tyne to the Solway Firth.

mix.q: What fruit does Crash Bandicoot collect throughout his classic video game series?
mix.why: Crash collects Wumpa fruit to earn extra lives across the franchise.

mix.q: Which album by Michael Jackson, released in 1982, became the best-selling album of all time?
mix.why: Thriller yielded seven top-10 singles and has sold over 70 million copies worldwide.

mix.q: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
mix.why: Diamond scores a maximum 10 on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.
